@graph.description: Welcome to Poonam Restaurant, where we serve delicious food with the warmth of Banarasi hospitality. Our menu includes a variety of dishes, from traditional Banarasi flavors to popular Indian and international meals. Every dish is prepared with fresh ingredients to give you the best taste and quality. Whether you are craving local favorites or looking to try something new, we have something for everyone. @graph.name: Explore Varanasi with Hotel Pradeep
@graph.description: Discover Varanasi's temples, ghats and heritage sites, with practical destination guides from Hotel Pradeep.

@graph.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
@graph.description: Dedicated to Lord Shiva, Kashi Vishwanath is one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines and a spiritual centre of the city. Its golden spires and the Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor connect the temple experience with the sacred riverfront. The surrounding lanes offer a close encounter with the everyday traditions of old Kashi.

@graph.caption: Ganga Dwar, the gateway to Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi
@graph.creditText: Ashvin Kaitabhya, clicked by Abhishek Pandey
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
@graph.description: One of Varanasi's best-known riverfront landmarks, Dashashwamedh Ghat brings together pilgrims, boats, and the energy of the old city. It is especially associated with the evening Ganga Aarti, when lamps, bells, and prayers create an unforgettable riverside atmosphere. A daytime visit reveals a different, equally absorbing rhythm of life along the steps.

@graph.caption: Dashashwamedh Ghat on the Ganges in Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Assi Ghat
@graph.description: At the southern end of the city's celebrated riverfront, Assi Ghat offers space to pause and watch the Ganges. Early mornings bring gentle light and a slower pace, while the surrounding neighbourhood has cafés and places to sit between walks. It is a welcoming starting point for experiencing the ghats beyond the busiest central stretch.

@graph.caption: Morning prayer ceremony at Assi Ghat in Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Sarnath
@graph.description: Sarnath is a major Buddhist pilgrimage destination associated with the Buddha's first teaching after enlightenment. The Dhamek Stupa, archaeological remains, and the nearby museum offer another perspective on the region's spiritual history. Its open grounds and historic monuments make a thoughtful contrast to the movement and intensity of the old city.

@graph.caption: The Dhamek Stupa at Sarnath near Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Ramnagar Fort
@graph.description: Across the Ganges from the old city, the eighteenth-century Ramnagar Fort introduces visitors to Varanasi's royal heritage. Its river-facing walls, courtyards, and historic setting offer a different view of the city. The museum collections add context to the lives, tastes, and traditions associated with the former royal household.

@graph.caption: Ramnagar Fort on the bank of the Ganges near Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: New Vishwanath Temple, BHU
@graph.description: Set within Banaras Hindu University, the New Vishwanath Temple is a distinctive landmark dedicated to Lord Shiva. Its tall spire and campus setting offer an experience quite different from the narrow lanes around Kashi Vishwanath. A visit can be combined with a gentle exploration of the university's tree-lined surroundings.

@graph.caption: The New Vishwanath Temple on the Banaras Hindu University campus
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Durga Kund Temple
@graph.description: Recognisable by its red exterior and North Indian temple towers, Durga Kund is dedicated to Goddess Durga. The temple and its adjacent water tank form one of the city's familiar devotional landmarks. It is a rewarding addition to a southern Varanasi visit, alongside nearby temples and the wider Assi neighbourhood.

@graph.caption: The red Durga Kund Temple and its adjacent water tank in Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.

@graph.name: Namo Ghat
@graph.description: Namo Ghat offers a contemporary addition to Varanasi's riverfront, with open public spaces and distinctive folded-hands sculptures. It provides a fresh perspective on the Ganges and an interesting contrast to the older, densely built ghats. Come for an unhurried walk and a wider view of the riverfront.

@graph.caption: The Ganges and Malviya Bridge viewed from Namo Ghat in Varanasi
@graph.description: WebP resizing and dedicated mobile crops applied to the credited source photograph.
